what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to grant a special permit reducing the minimum lot size at 32 Spring Street so a new single-family house can be built.
The lot-size problem surfaced after a zoning district split between RA and RB was found on the property, following an earlier ANR plan that had already been endorsed.
The board left the boundary of the septic-system area where the plan showed it, though the applicant's engineer said its exact placement had some flexibility.
No members of the public attended or commented on the petition.
The chair read the standard conditions and appeal rights attached to the special permit after the vote.

why_it_matters: The permit allows a smaller lot than the bylaw normally requires so a new house can be built, based on a septic system serving the neighboring house at 31 Spring Street sitting partly on this lot.

The case shows how a zoning district boundary running through a property can create a lot-size problem even after an earlier plan for the same land was already approved, which matters to anyone splitting or building on property near a district line.
